children: Malaysian palm oil futures extended losses for a fourth straight session on Friday and were on track for a third weekly decline in four weeks, as weaker rival edible oils weighed on the market.
The benchmark palm oil contract
for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange slid 33 ringgit, or 0.76%, to 4,300 ringgit ($1,046.23) a metric ton in early trade. The contract has lost 2.11% so far this week.
FUNDAMENTALS
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) fell 0.41%, while its palm oil contract
shed 1.16%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade
were down 0.22%.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Oil prices edged higher, though set for a weekly decline, as concerns over supply disruptions grew following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. O/R
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
The ringgit
, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.02% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.

Indonesian state-owned palm plantation company Agrinas Palma Nusantara aims to transfer control of more than 200,000 hectares of land it manages to local cooperatives next year, a company director said.
Palm oil may test a resistance at 4,391 ringgit per metric ton, a break above could lead to a gain into the 4,663-4,507 ringgit range, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said. TECH/C
MARKET NEWS

Asian shares slid on Friday, putting them on track for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic's ANT.O debut failed to restore investor faith in AI trades, while the dollar extended its rally on safe-haven flows. MKTS/GLOB
